item.title: [7.1] Global Market: Bank of Japan achieves 2% inflation target after 13 years
item.description:
WHAT HAPPENED

The Bank of Japan declared its long-standing 2% inflation target achieved after more than 13 years, but kept its benchmark interest rate unchanged at 1.25%. Persistent inflation, rising oil and semiconductor prices, and yen weakness have fuelled expectations of another rate hike in December as policymakers gradually tighten monetary policy.

WHY IT MATTERS

Declaring the 2% inflation target achieved after 13 years marks a historic structural shift for Japan's economy and global capital flows, with explicit signals of a December rate hike.
